Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Bay and sea scallops

Fall scalloping is remembered as a much-anticipated part of Shinnecock food life. The catalogue records concern about poorer bay-scallop harvests in the years before 2014. It also describes decorative uses of bay-scallop shells and sea-scallop shells used as scoops.1

The sea-scallop entry names the Atlantic and southern Long Island; the other named bays belong to the bay-scallop entry.1

Places named in the catalogue

Peconic Bay; Great South Bay; Shinnecock Bay; Heady Crick; Napeague Bay; Long Island Sound; Atlantic Ocean.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 5. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
